mainEntity.name: How long should I wait after tooth extraction before having an implant placed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The waiting period varies depending on individual circumstances and clinical factors. Simple extractions may allow implant placement within 8-12 weeks, whilst complex cases or those requiring additional healing may need 3-6 months. Your dental professional will assess your specific situation to determine optimal timing based on bone healing, tissue recovery, and overall oral health status.

mainEntity.name: Can dental implants be placed immediately after tooth extraction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate implant placement is possible in suitable cases where specific clinical conditions are met. The extraction site must be infection-free, adequate bone must be present, and primary implant stability must be achievable. Not all extractions are suitable for immediate placement, and your dental professional will evaluate whether this approach offers the best outcome for your situation.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I wait too long before getting a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Extended delays after tooth loss can result in bone resorption and changes to the surrounding teeth positioning. However, implants can still often be placed successfully even years after tooth loss, though additional procedures such as bone grafting may be required. Early consultation allows discussion of timing options and any additional treatments that might be beneficial.

mainEntity.name: Does age affect the timing of dental implant placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age itself doesn't typically prevent successful implant treatment, though individual healing capacity and overall health status are important considerations. Younger patients generally heal faster, whilst older patients may require slightly longer healing periods. The timing approach is tailored to individual circumstances rather than age alone, focusing on optimising conditions for successful treatment.

mainEntity.name: How does smoking affect dental implant timing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smoking significantly impairs healing and increases the risk of implant complications. Smokers may require extended healing periods before implant placement and face higher risks of treatment failure. Many dental professionals recommend smoking cessation before implant treatment, and timing decisions often incorporate strategies to optimise healing in patients who smoke.

mainEntity.name: Can other dental problems affect when implants should be placed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, existing oral health conditions such as gum disease, infection, or inadequate oral hygiene may require treatment before implant placement. Periodontal treatment or management of other dental conditions often takes priority to establish stable oral health. This helps support optimal conditions for successful implant integration and long-term maintenance.
